newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia stocks end lower after sharp slide.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia stocks end lower after sharp slide.

text.p: SPI Sycom cl 2426 -33.0 US 30yr cl 6.81 +0.03
10yrbond futs 92.285 -0.030 Gold NY 358.65 Lon fix 360.00
AUD US$0.7755 (Thur $0.7756) CRB Index cl 242.72 -0.17
*Stocks end lower after sharp slide caused by arbitrage trading between physical and futures. Volume 565.53 million, value A$1.63 bln, 1,158 stocks traded, 336 steady, 384 up, 438 down.

Australian shares ended lower on Friday after arbitrage trading between the futures and physical market caused both markets to fall sharply, before further investor buying steadied some pre-weeked nerves.
At 4.30 p.m. (0530 GMT), the All Ordinaries index ended 14.8 points lower at 2,449.9 points after falling nearly 30 points in a late afternoon flurry.
The index had spent most of the day almost paralysed.
The March share price index futures contract was 33 points down at 2,426 off its Friday low of 2,422, widening the discount to the underlying index to 27.9 points.
"There is some arbitrage trading going on," said Rodney Green chief investment officer at Perpetual Funds Management.
"The futures have fallen away, as the discount was widening, so people were buying futures and selling physical," Green said.
The futures market had been around a four point discount to the physical market at midday.

Green said investors were getting a little nervous before the weekend, particularly as overseas markets are still digesting the hawkish comments made by Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan made to the Senate Banking Committee on Wednesday.
"I think the Greenspan comments over the past couple of days has made people a little nervous. People are probably thinking they don't want to take the risk over the weekend," Green said.
Trade was largely dominated by the end of the months options expires, with a lot of the trade done before the market open.
Base metals miner Pasminco Ltd, Rupert Murdoch's News Corp Ltd and building materials group Boral Ltd were the most actively traded amongst the majors.
A higher gold price and firmer base metal prices helped push up resource share prices. The gold index recorded the strongest move by any local sector and the media sector was the weakest.
Brambles Industries fuelled the corporate earnings charge on Friday with a 14.3 percent rise in first half net profit, but its shares remained steady at A$21.70.
While the rest of the results were mixed.
Gold miner Acacia Resources and paper group Spicers Paper both reporting lower profits, while metal fabrication group G.E. Crane and fruit canning group SPC both reported higher profits.
Falls outnumbered rises by 11 to 10, while about 30 percent of stocks traded were steady.
In other local markets, the Australian debt market ended slightly weaker in a relatively subdued session as it braced itself for what could prove to be another volatile trading week.
At 5.10 p.m. (0610 GMT), the 10 year T-bonds were yielding 7.70 percent, up from Thursday's 7.67 percent.
The Australian dollar ended on a steady note, which belied a choppy. At 5.10 p.m. (0610 GMT), the dollar was US$0.7750/57.
